components.implementation: Splunk Enterprise with Splunk Universal Forwarder
inputs: raw logs from endpoints and IDS
components.name: SIEM indexing
components.role: collect and index security logs

components.implementation: fixed 5-minute windows; mean/max of ports and bytes, IPs, protocol
components.name: Data cleaning and feature extraction
components.role: deduplicate events and build windowed features

components.implementation: reconstruction autoencoder |F|->8->2->8->|F|, MSE error, trained benign-only on the first 25% of the timeline
components.name: Autoencoder anomaly detector
components.role: score how unusual a window is

components.implementation: PPO-trained 2x64 MLP with ReLU and softmax
components.name: DRL triage policy
components.role: decide Allow vs Contain per window

components.implementation: priority = action x score; forward only when above threshold (5)
components.name: Triage and prioritization
components.role: gate which windows reach the LLM

components.implementation: CrewAI with Senior SOC Triage Analyst, Threat Intelligence Analyst, and Orchestrator; verbatim role prompts
components.name: LLM multi-agent layer
components.role: produce risk assessment, SPL queries, and ATT&CK mapping

components.implementation: human analyst runs SPL in read-only mode
components.name: Splunk verification + human decision
components.role: validate generated SPL against real logs and make the call

memory.details: No persistent store; per-window feature vectors are recomputed from raw logs, plus a SOC-scoped anonymization mapping table.

architecture.orchestration: strict sequential pipeline with two gates: DRL window filter, then priority threshold before the LLM; human is final decision authority; the anomaly score is deliberately excluded from the DRL state to prevent feature leakage; pseudonymization applied before any LLM call with a reversible SOC-side placeholder mapping

datasets: BOSS of the SOC (BOTS) subset (~12k instances)
custom simulated corpus (300k instances, Kali -> Windows 11)
evaluation.reported_results: BOTS: mode B F1 0.861, recall 0.873; simulated corpus: mode D precision 0.926, recall 0.696, F1 0.795 with the lowest regret 1.358; ~63-65% reduction in traffic forwarded to the LLM

limitations: Fixed 5-minute windows can miss short-lived attacks
Binary action space (Allow/Contain) only; no monitor/throttle/escalate
No RAG or vector store; context management is funneling-only
No retry or fallback logic documented for LLM or SPL failures
Read-only by design; all mitigation executed by humans (intentional)
Dataset scale and diversity limited; single-attacker simulation
Local-LLM accuracy and hallucination risk untested
papers.title: Policy-Guided Threat Hunting: An LLM enabled Framework with Splunk SOC Triage

components.implementation: reasoning-class LLM with plan-then-execute (PtE) and PS+ prompting, anchored to an ATT&CK-derived task tree
components.name: Planner
components.role: build and maintain the investigation plan

components.implementation: cheap-model specialists (recon, scan, exploit, report) with wrappers such as nmap_scan(ip_address) and run_code(python_script)
components.name: Executor agents
components.role: run subtasks and call tools

components.implementation: finite-state machine / task graph / PTT / TCG (e.g., AutoPT FSM, PentestGPT PTT, VulnBot graph, xOffense TCG)
components.name: Structured state
components.role: track plan state between agents

components.implementation: static and dynamic analysis filters between agent output and tool execution
components.name: Deterministic verification layer
components.role: check AI claims against real tools before use

components.implementation: manual review plus enrollment scoping and rules of engagement
components.name: Human approval gate
components.role: authorize destructive actions

components.implementation: two-tier: context window plus vector DB/RAG with summarization, pruning, and HTML minification
components.name: Memory
components.role: provide long-term context

memory.details: Two-tier memory: short-term context window plus long-term vector DB / RAG with summarization, pruning, and HTML minification; memory-poisoning risks highlighted.

architecture.orchestration: plan-then-execute loop with a reasoning-tier planner and cheap executors; per-stage tool-call and token budgets; checkpointed replanning on failure; deterministic verification between agent output and tool execution; human approval gates for destructive actions; sandboxed containers

evaluation.reported_results: NYU CTF Bench 2026: Claude 4.5 Opus 59%, Gemini 3 Pro 52%, +9.5 points with a Kali tool environment; AIxCC finalists found 54/63 (86%) synthetic vulnerabilities and patched 43 (68%) across 5.4M LoC plus 18 real-world vulnerabilities; IRIS found 55 vs CodeQL 27; guided task-tree completion 71.8-78.6% vs 13.5-16.5% self-guided; AutoPT $0.024/test, RapidPen $0.30-0.60/test

limitations: CTF benchmarks do not equal production (authorization, rate limits, ambiguous success)
Hallucination documented: invented file paths, misread forms, inferred nonexistent control flow
Indirect prompt injection via untrusted page and log content; tool, memory, and RAG poisoning
Containment imperfect in practice (shared kernels, metadata services; Clinejection incident hit ~4,000 developers)
Context limits and lost-in-the-middle; retrieval failures can omit crucial evidence
Reasoning-class model costs 5-20x per token
Dual-use: scoped defensive prompts trivially repurposable
papers.title: LLM-Based Intelligent Agents for Cybersecurity: A Tutorial and Survey of Automated Vulnerability Discovery

components.implementation: LLM with reasoning module, task decomposition, and explicit decision-making logic
components.name: LLM core agent
components.role: reference supervisor: reason, decompose tasks, and decide the next action

components.implementation: threat intel database, historical attack data, MITRE ATT&CK, organizational context; RAG and vector/knowledge stores recommended
components.name: Knowledge sources
components.role: supply grounding context for reasoning

components.implementation: network scanner, log analyzer, vulnerability scanner, SIEM integration, incident response
components.name: Tool executors
components.role: touch external systems on behalf of the agent

components.implementation: human-in-the-loop escalation on high-confidence threat or impasse; TRiSM-managed multi-agent escalation
components.name: Monitoring and feedback loop
components.role: human oversight and continuous learning

memory.details: RAG and vector stores recommended for long-term knowledge (historical attack data, behavioral profiles, ATT&CK); short-term conversational context; knowledge graphs for campaign-level correlation.

architecture.orchestration: knowledge-based execution loop: hypothesize -> query data sources -> analyze -> iterate; escalate to a human only on a high-confidence threat or an impasse, with confidence thresholding

evaluation.reported_results: Cross-study synthesis (Table 4): binary classification AUC 0.90-0.97, F1 0.85-0.94; TTP identification precision 0.75-0.88, recall 0.68-0.82; IoT detection accuracy 0.82-0.91; CTI extraction precision 0.80-0.92; incident-timeline ordering 0.85-0.93

limitations: Systematic review, so no implementation or artifacts of its own
Heterogeneous metrics across surveyed studies limit direct comparison
Rare TTPs under-recalled (18-32% missed)
Prompt injection, data poisoning (1-5%), and poor confidence calibration remain exploitable
Benchmark-to-production gap; few longitudinal operational SOC deployments
Fine-tuning cost (tens of thousands of USD for GPT-3-class models) and RAG latency (2-5x)

components.implementation: graph attention network fused with transformer-based sequence modeling
components.name: Detector agent
components.role: finds behavioral anomalies in process execution chains

components.implementation: reinforcement-learning policy (PPO-style, AutoHunt referenced as prior art)
components.name: Hunter agent
components.role: prioritizes high-value investigation paths during hunting

components.implementation: LLM (model unspecified)
components.name: LLM orchestrator
components.role: synthesizes narratives, emits low-false-positive alerts, and generates remediation playbooks

components.implementation: reflective autonomy loop (Reflexion-like)
components.name: Critic module
components.role: reviews past actions and adjusts future strategy

components.implementation: SOAR platform running autonomously
components.name: SOAR integration
components.role: executes remediation playbooks

memory.details: No memory mechanism is described in the paper.

architecture.orchestration: phased pipeline with a feedback loop: detect -> prioritize -> narrate -> execute via SOAR; the critic feeds lessons back into detectors and policies; micro-segmentation policy refreshed roughly every 90 seconds; high-stakes decisions reserved for human approval

evaluation.reported_results: F1 0.93 / AUC 0.98 vs XGBoost 0.77 (Table 1); MTTR reduced 45.1 to 7.8 minutes; containment by ATT&CK phase 97/89/91/88% vs baseline SOAR 68/51/39/42% (Table 2); analyst trust 72%

limitations: No prompts, code, or artifacts published despite claiming a reproducible methodology
No hallucination guardrails described
Autonomous SOAR execution without a documented sandbox or read-only API posture
Black-box decision pathways; only 72% analyst trust even after SHAP/counterfactual exposure
Adversarial robustness untested; the paper's own literature review reports 78% of tested LLM defense policies bypassable via jailbreaks
Memory and retrieval strategy undefined
papers.title: Agentic AI and Cyber Security: Autonomous Threat Hunting, Intrusion Detection, and Adaptive Defense Mechanisms in a World of Increasingly Sophisticated Cyber Attacks
